subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-agent delegate-only tool policy such as `tools.selfDeny`, solve this through the open per-spawn `toolsAllow` direction, or reject delegate-only inheritance to preserve strict parent-as-upper-bound semantics?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this is a public config and security-boundary decision that automation should not settle without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy only after maintainers define naming, denial precedence, subagent inheritance semantics, docs, and security tests.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn toolsAllow
options.body: Treat the open per-spawn allowlist work as the supported solution and document that parent direct-use prevention still needs separate profiles or future work.

options.title: Reject delegate-only inheritance
options.body: Keep strict parent-as-upper-bound semantics and document separate-agent or per-spawn restriction patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Design delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy only after maintainers define naming, denial precedence, subagent inheritance semantics, docs, and security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing review context already routes the unresolved public API/security-boundary decision to steipete, and no narrower code-owner signal overrides that product decision need.
